sections.title: Most relevant source
sections.body_markdown:
**Hydrophobic residue substitutions enhance the stability and in vivo immunogenicity of respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein.** [9]

Song Q, Yang H, Zhu H et al. Hydrophobic residue substitutions enhance the stability and in vivo immunogenicity of respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein. *Journal of virology* 2025 (doi:10.1128/jvi.00087-25; PMID 40434102; PMC12172430)

Relevance grade 3/3 · in_vivo, in_vitro · read from full text
Its own experiments changed: **pre-F-IFLP** (name checked against the abstract)

> Hydrophobic residue substitutions enhance the stability and in vivo immunogenicity of respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein.

Why it ranks first: The paper reports that introducing four hydrophobic residue substitutions into the RSV F protein resulted in a highly stable prefusion F trimer (pre-F-IFLP) with improved expression levels in cultured cells and superior stability compared to DS-Cav1, the first-generation prefusion F-stabilized RSV-1

sections.title: Gaps and caveats
sections.body_markdown:
- Papers were read for **safety liabilities**, but no verified finding was extracted.
- 3 of 11 papers read were available as abstract only.
- Figures and tables are not read: results reported only in a figure are not in this report.
- 8 collected paper(s) were excluded as being about something close to, but not, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection (BRSV, Bovine Respiratory Syncytial Virus, Bovine respiratory syncytial virus, HMPV).
- 1 drafted sentence(s) were removed because they stated something their cited evidence does not.
- Targets are ordered by: papers with human clinical evidence of benefit, then papers with human genetic evidence, then papers with animal evidence of benefit, then the number of independent papers. This counts kinds of evidence; it does not judge any paper's quality.

sections.title: How this answer was assembled
sections.body_markdown:
- **Collected:** 82 papers from the searcher.
- **Exact-entity gate:** 62 passed; 8 about a near-miss; 0 not about the subject; 12 reviews; 0 retracted.
- **Relevance:** 40 papers graded by the model from title and abstract; the rest ranked lexically.
- **Read:** 11 papers, chosen by the evidence plan.
- **Extracted:** 178 findings proposed; 1 discarded because their quote is not in the paper; 3 discarded as about another entity; 19 duplicates merged; **74 verified findings kept**.
- **Written:** 53 sentences kept; 1 removed by the citation check; 19 removed as repeats; 2 too short to state anything.
- Every sentence cites the findings it relies on, and every finding's quote was matched word for word against its paper. Numbers and names in each sentence were checked against the evidence it cites.

evidence.effect_detail: All three hospitalized RSV cases occurred in term infants. Unvaccinated infant had severe disease requiring invasive ventilation. Both nirsevimab recipients had markedly milder illness.
evidence.quote: The clinical severity patterns differed across seasons, although small case numbers precluded statistical comparisons. During nirsevimab implementation (2024–2025), all three hospitalized RSV cases occurred in term infants with distinct outcomes stratified by vaccination status. The single unvaccinated infant developed severe disease requiring 2 days of invasive ventilation, with moderate clinical severity, and bilateral opacities on chest X-ray. In contrast, both nirsevimab recipients experienced markedly milder illness: one required only brief non-invasive respiratory support, while the other one needed no ventilatory assistance, with both showing minimal radiological perihilar changes.
